title: Which is greater, a four digit or a five digit number?
description: Joseph counts the visitors at a village fair on two days. The video counts the digits of both numbers and finds which is greater.
teaching_notes: One idea: count the digits first; the number with more digits is greater. Watch for children who compare the first digits only.

video_script.why: The child compares numbers with the same number of digits and now meets numbers of different lengths.
video_script.substitution: Count the digits first; a number with more digits is greater whatever its first digit.
video_script.anchor: Joseph's count of visitors on two days of a village fair
video_script.wrong_answer: nine thousand eight hundred seventy six is greater
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu compares the first digits, nine and one, and picks the number that starts with nine. The two digits sit in different places.

final_answer.spoken: ten thousand twelve is greater than nine thousand eight hundred seventy six

never_show: the your-turn answer: 12,000 is greater than 8,450
maths_rules: first number 9,876 has 4 digits; second number 10,012 has 5 digits
the fifth place from the right is the ten thousands place; the leading 1 there is worth 10,000
the greatest 4-digit number is 9,999, which is less than 10,000, so 10,012 > 9,876
slip: 9 > 1 compares digits that sit in different places
your turn: 8,450 has 4 digits, 12,000 has 5 digits; 12,000 > 8,450; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: more digits means greater. Wrong idea: the bigger first digit wins. Two rows of boxes sit on the place value chart, one box for each digit.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which of these two counts is the greater number?

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Count the digits first.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Nine thousand eight hundred seventy six has four digits, and ten thousand twelve has five digits.
<bookmark mark='extra'/>The extra place on the left is the ten thousands place, and it holds a one.
<bookmark mark='big'/>That one is worth ten thousand, and no four digit number reaches ten thousand.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Ten thousand twelve is greater, even though nine is greater than one.
